overview:
CA-49 along the San Diego-area coast leans Democratic by seven points, and incumbent Mike Levin is seeking another term against Republican Armen Kurdian. The structural picture favors Levin: the district's partisan lean, the benefits of incumbency, and a national environment credited to Democrats all point the same direction. No public general-election polls are available, so the outlook rests on fundamentals rather than survey evidence.

Money tells a lopsided story. Levin has raised roughly $3.5 million and holds about $1.45 million on hand, while Kurdian has raised under $60,000 with minimal outside support on either side. Betting markets on Kalshi and Polymarket both put Levin's chances around 96 to 97 percent. The seat rates as Safe Democratic, though the lack of polling keeps uncertainty wider than in well-surveyed contests.
